entries.title: Fossil fuel impasse pushes COP31 climate talks into second day of overtime
entries.summary: COP31 President ​Murat Kurum asks negotiators to consider a last-minute proposal in attempt to reach an agreement.
entries.content:
COP31 President ​Murat Kurum asks negotiators to consider a last-minute proposal in attempt to reach an agreement.

Turkish officials have asked negotiators at the COP31 climate summit to consider a last-minute proposal as talks stretched into a second day of overtime over the fossil fuels issue.

“We believe that we have put forward a text which all the parties can agree upon,” COP31 President Murat Kurum told a late-night plenary session on Saturday.

Kurum, who is also Turkiye’s environment minister, said the conference would reconvene later on Sunday morning to approve the deal.

The latest text was not immediately made public, and it was unclear if negotiators had received the wording overnight, which would give nations only a few hours to submit objections and changes.

An earlier draft had drawn strong condemnation for failing to mention fossil fuels, the largest contributors to climate change.

Kurum said he ⁠believed concerns around fossil fuels had ‌been addressed, as had those ‌around helping developing countries finance their adaptations to climate change.

The new ‌text followed intensive consultations between Australia, which is ‌leading the talks; Turkiye, which is hosting the meeting; and nearly 200 delegations from many of the world’s richest, poorest, largest and smallest nations.

Delegations had until 03:00 GMT on Sunday to ‌raise any objections to the deal, with a session scheduled at 06:00 GMT to ⁠begin approving ⁠it.

The summit’s agreement is meant to address how the world will deal with climate change, which drives heatwaves, floods and other disasters.

An opening draft from Australia on Monday called for a faster phase-out of fossil fuels. A slimmer version on Thursday removed every mention of them after Saudi Arabia and other major oil and gas producers objected.

Key issues that slowed down the agreement included how much effort countries should make to wean themselves off fossil fuels, such as coal, oil and gas.

Other issues included whether to encourage industrial carbon capture and storage of pollutants, as well as whether ramping up electricity should only be done with renewables, such as wind and solar, or also involve other sources like natural gas and coal.

To avert the most catastrophic effects of warming, experts said the world needs to urgently and drastically cut fossil fuel emissions.

The two-week talks in the Turkish city of Antalya were due to end on Friday.

In a letter sent on Saturday to this year’s cohosts, Turkiye and Australia, 100 civil society groups warned that they were “on course to preside over one of the most disappointing COPs” the UN has ever held.

The letter stated there were only hours left “to save this COP from becoming a low point of three decades of climate negotiations”.

In the lead-up to these talks, the United Nations said the world would likely blow past the 2015 Paris Agreement goal of limiting warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) above pre-industrial temperatures.

entries.title: Eleven killed in burst of violence during Mexican cartel leader’s capture
entries.summary: Seven alleged cartel gunmen and four soldiers were killed in operation to arrest cartel boss Fausto Isidro Meza Flores.
entries.content:
Seven alleged cartel gunmen and four soldiers were killed in the operation to arrest Fausto Isidro Meza Flores.

The operation to capture Mexican cartel boss Fausto Isidro Meza Flores in the country’s Sinaloa state has left at least 11 people dead.

Mexico’s Defence Ministry said on Saturday that seven alleged cartel gunmen and four Mexican soldiers were killed in the overnight operation.

Meza Flores, known as “El Chapo Isidro”, was captured on Friday and flown to Mexico City on Saturday after hours-long violence involving a firefight between Mexican forces and cartel gunmen overnight, roadblocks and burning trucks in the city of Guasave.

Two other men were also captured and flown to Mexico City. The ministry identified them as German N, known as “Serafin”, the group’s alleged second-in-command, and Jose N, an alleged financial operator of the cartel. Both were also flown to Mexico City and handed over to prosecutors.

Meza Flores, one of the FBI’s 10 most wanted fugitives, climbed the ranks to lead the Beltrán Leyva cartel and later became the boss of his own group, the Meza-Flores transnational criminal organisation.

He was also a key ally to “Los Mayos”, a faction of the Sinaloa Cartel, which the United States designated as a “foreign terrorist organization” last year.

The US wanted Meza Flores for trafficking drugs to the country and offered a $5m reward for information leading to his arrest.

Residents terrified

The firefight in Guasave broke out about 7pm on Friday (02:00 GMT on Saturday), according to residents. Military helicopters and drones were soon flying overhead, with helicopters opening fire on key locations across the city.

Videos show screaming civilians fleeing gunfire at a baseball game, burning cars and businesses, and circling helicopters shooting at people below.

Because of the violence, the Mexican army and National Guard special forces were unable to extract Meza Flores from Guasave until 4am (11:00 GMT) on Saturday, said a federal official who spoke on condition of anonymity because he was not authorised to discuss the case.

While a tense calm has settled over Guasave since the operation, experts warned that picking off cartel bosses could set off more waves of violence in a region already caught up in a power struggle between warring factions.

Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum has been under pressure from US President Donald Trump to crack down on cartels and has gone after illegal groups more aggressively than her predecessors. Homicides have dipped significantly in her two years in office.

The US Drug Enforcement Administration commended Mexican authorities, as did Washington’s ambassador to Mexico.

“Results like these don’t happen overnight. They are built on sustained cooperation and trust. This is what partners can accomplish together,” US Ambassador Ronald Johnson said in an X post.

entries.title: Overturned boat carrying mourners to funeral kills at least 24 in Nigeria
entries.summary: Police say the boat driver fled and the vessel’s manager was taken into custody.
entries.content:
Police say the boat driver fled and the vessel’s manager was taken into custody.

A boat believed to be carrying hundreds of attendees to a funeral has overturned in southern Nigeria, killing at least 24 people, according to authorities.

The overcrowded vessel capsized on Friday in Bayelsa State after a mechanical failure while travelling from the communities of Ayama to Ukubie, according to police.

“So far, 24 bodies have been recovered from the scene of the incident, while search and rescue operations are ongoing,” Manzo Ezekiel, a spokesman for the National Emergency Management Agency, said on Saturday.

Rescue and search operations were continuing, he added.

Two children were among the four bodies initially recovered from the water on Friday, police said at the time, adding that 24 people were rescued, with 19 treated at a local clinic and five taken to hospital in the state capital.

Police did not say how many people were on board, but some residents told the Reuters news agency there were at least 300.

Police said the driver fled and the vessel’s manager was taken into custody.

According to a statement from the Bayelsa State Police Command, the accident occurred at the river junction between the Oweikorogha and Otuan communities, in the state’s Southern Ijaw district.

The boat that capsized was travelling “for a burial ceremony”, the statement also said, adding that police are “coordinating efforts with local divers and other responders”.

Such boat accidents are common on Nigeria’s busy rivers and waterways, often caused by overloaded vessels, poor maintenance, or failure to comply with safety regulations.

A similar incident occurred in August, when at least 51 people died after a boat sank in northwest Nigeria’s Sokoto State. In another incident, in January, at least 26 people drowned after a boat ferrying people from Jigawa to Yobe State capsized.

entries.title: Displaced Palestinians protest as Israeli air strikes continue in Gaza
entries.summary: Israeli forces continue to destroy residential buildings as part of a 'gradual displacement' policy, a Gaza mayor says.
entries.content:
Israeli forces continue to destroy residential buildings as part of a ‘gradual displacement’ policy, a Gaza mayor says.

Hundreds of displaced Palestinians have protested as Israeli forces continue to destroy residential buildings in Gaza, beyond the line they withdrew to under last year’s ceasefire.

Al Jazeera journalist Moath al-Kahlout, reporting from Gaza’s Deir el-Balah, said displaced Palestinians who live in the area near the “Yellow Line” gathered on Saturday to demonstrate against Israel’s intensifying air strikes.

The “Yellow Line” separates Israeli- and Hamas-controlled areas in Gaza since the “ceasefire” signed in October 2025.

“More than 500 housing units have been destroyed in less than a month,” said Mohammed Musleh, mayor of Deir-el Balah’s Maghazi municipality, told Al Jazeera.

“This is part of what appears to be a systematic policy of gradual creeping displacement aimed at forcing residents out of their camp and destroying as many homes as possible,” Musleh said.

Gaza’s Ministry of Public Works and Housing says 350,000 families are homeless after Israeli attacks destroyed 80 percent of the enclave’s homes.

Meanwhile, flooding in recent weeks devastated temporary tent housing, the ministry said.

The original “Yellow Line”, established under US President Donald Trump’s 20-point plan to end Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, marked the area to which Israeli forces initially withdrew. They were expected to make further withdrawals gradually, but instead seized more territory.

“If we go back to October 2025, when the ceasefire was signed, the ‘Yellow Line’ was much further east,” al-Kahlout said.

Now, nearly two-thirds of Gaza is under Israeli army control or subject to access restrictions.

Rising death toll

Israeli attacks killed at least four Palestinians in Gaza on Saturday, including three who died when an Israeli drone struck a van delivering food aid to displaced people in Gaza City.

In the past 48 hours, Israeli strikes killed at least nine people, taking the death toll since the October 2025 “ceasefire” to 1,661, according to the latest report from Gaza’s Ministry of Health.

The ministry said 55 Palestinians were wounded in the past 48 hours, putting the total number of the wounded since October 2025 at 6,062.

More than 100 remains recovered

Gaza’s Civil Defence said on Saturday that its crew members recovered the bodies and remains of 129 people from 39 homes and other Israeli-destroyed buildings in the Nuseirat refugee camp, az-Zawayda and Deir el-Balah in central Gaza.

Rami al-Aidi, Civil Defence director in central Gaza, said 233 people had been reported missing beneath the rubble of those buildings.

The 53-day operation marked the conclusion of the second phase of a recovery project in central Gaza funded by the International Committee of the Red Cross.

Gaza’s Civil Defence said in October that about 8,000 bodies remained under the rubble across the enclave, including about 4,000 in Israeli-controlled areas. The agency warned that recovery could take eight to 10 years with the equipment available.

entries.title: Lebanese president demands Israel withdrawal, decries Iran’s interference
entries.summary: Joseph Aoun says 'two fundamental obstacles, inseparably linked' mean Lebanon cannot fully celebrate its independence.
entries.content:
Joseph Aoun says ‘two fundamental obstacles, inseparably linked’ mean Lebanon cannot fully celebrate its independence.

Lebanese President Joseph Aoun has decried Iran’s meddling in Lebanon’s affairs and demanded Israel’s withdrawal from his country’s south.

In a speech on Saturday, on the eve of Lebanon’s 83rd independence anniversary, Aoun said Lebanon faces two interconnected fateful tests: the “Israeli occupation of parts of our land” and “foreign interference” from “some influential parties in the Iranian regime” through weapons and decisions outside the authority of the Lebanese state.

These “two fundamental obstacles, inseparably linked” mean that Lebanon cannot fully celebrate its independence, he added.

“Withdraw from every inch of Lebanese territory. Stop your attacks. And return our captives,” Aoun demanded of Israel.

Dozens of Lebanese citizens are believed to be held in Israeli detention centres, including civilians as well as members of the Hezbollah armed group captured during fighting in southern Lebanon.

The president also pledged to press ahead with plans to bring all weapons under state control, declaring that there would be “no weapons outside the state that take orders from, or serve the interests of foreign powers.”

“You must hand over your weapons,” Aoun said.

Lebanon’s government has promised to disarm Hezbollah, the Iran-backed Lebanese group whose arsenal has long outstripped that of the national army and that has justified its weapons as necessary to resist Israel.

Lebanon and Israel signed a framework agreement in June, following US-mediated talks, which included the disarmament of Hezbollah, a gradual Israeli withdrawal from southern Lebanese territories and the deployment of the Lebanese army to the area.

But implementation has stalled, with Hezbollah refusing to surrender its weapons and Israel continuing to strike Lebanon.

Israeli strikes

On Saturday, Israeli strikes hit the districts of Nabatieh, Bint Jbeil and Marjayoun in southern Lebanon.

Al Jazeera correspondents reported that one of the air strikes hit the outskirts of Baraachit, a town in Bint Jbeil.

They said Baraachit came under Israeli gunfire at dawn and reported the movement of Israeli military vehicles on the outskirts of the town.

Israeli warplanes launched a second missile attack on the town of Kfar Tebnit in Nabatieh, after the first failed to detonate, according to Lebanon’s National News Agency (NNA).

The NNA reported that Israeli forces carried out three explosions in Wadi al-Khiam in the Marjayoun district, but gave no further details.

Israeli attacks in southern Lebanon have killed at least 4,386 people and wounded 12,407 others since March 2, when the latest Hezbollah-Israel war started.

Lebanon’s Ministry of Health said that since Israel began its genocidal war on Gaza in October 2023, Israeli strikes in Lebanon have killed 8,953 people and injured 30,643 others.
